implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control (P06) was approved 2026-08-31. No access control policy existed before. Account management and CUI share procedures are due 2026-11-30.

Accounts are created in the identity provider from HR onboarding tickets and federated to the ERP and email. The file server and ERP use named accounts. Gaps: the WMS handhelds use 6 shared zone accounts; terminations are processed by hand, usually within about 3 business days; accounts are not disabled after inactivity; there is no quarterly access review.
evidence: Identity provider user export; HR termination tickets; WMS user list

implementation_statement: The ERP enforces role-based access for sales, purchasing, warehouse, finance, and administration. Gap: about 140 CUI configuration documents sit in a general file share readable by all 62 domain users. The CUI enclave project moves them to a restricted CUI share for 9 named users by 2026-12-15.
evidence: ERP role matrix; file share permission report 2026-07-16

implementation_statement: Planned. CUI flows are not controlled today: 14 ERP sales orders carry CUI attachments, and the lab bench network sits on the corporate VLAN. Planned: purge ERP attachments on DoD orders and block new ones (2026-09-30), and a lab VLAN with deny-by-default rules to the CUI share (2026-12-15).
evidence: ERP attachment search 2026-07-17; network diagram draft

implementation_statement: The ERP separates purchase order entry (buyers) from supplier payment approval (Controller) and supplier master changes (Controller only). Gap: the Systems Administrator both administers systems and manages their logs.
Office users have no local administrator rights. Gaps: 9 ERP users hold administrator rights (target 2), and the 6 lab technicians are local administrators on lab workstations.
evidence: ERP administrator report; endpoint policy report

implementation_statement: The identity provider locks an account for 15 minutes after 10 failed sign-in attempts. This applies to every federated application.
Planned. No system use or CUI notice is shown today. A logon banner for Windows, the VPN, and the CUI share is due 2026-10-31.
Endpoint policy locks screens after 15 minutes idle with a pattern-hiding screen. Gap: the 6 lab workstations are exempt so long configuration jobs are not interrupted.
Identity provider sessions end after 12 hours; ERP sessions end after 60 minutes idle; VPN sessions end after 8 hours.
evidence: Identity provider and ERP session settings

implementation_statement: Remote access uses the firewall VPN with identity provider MFA; no other inbound services are open. Gaps: VPN sessions are not reviewed, split tunneling is allowed, and MSP remote access runs through its own RMM tool (SYS-13) without a written authorization.
Corporate Wi-Fi uses WPA2-Enterprise with identity provider accounts. Guest Wi-Fi is isolated. Gap: scanner Wi-Fi uses one shared pre-shared key, so devices are not individually authorized.
Company phones and personal phones can reach email. Gap: no mobile device management or app protection policy, and no rule against CUI on phones.
POL-05 (approved 2026-08-31) limits work to company systems. Gap: personal cloud storage sites are not blocked.
Only the Sales Operations Manager and one marketing coordinator can publish to the website and portal catalog. Content is reviewed before posting so it never includes CUI or FCI.
All staff watch a security awareness video at hire and each January. Gaps: no content on CUI, business email compromise, bank-change fraud, or insider threat; no phishing exercises.
Planned. No role-based training exists. Modules for lab technicians (CUI handling), receiving and buyers (anti-counterfeit and Section 889), and administrators are due 2026-12-15.

implementation_statement: Cloud audit logs, identity provider sign-in logs, firewall logs, and ERP audit trails are on with default settings. Gap: the events to log are not defined, and file server object access to the CUI share is not logged.
Log records include user, time, source address, event type, and outcome as generated by each service.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Planned. Nobody reviews logs today. Weekly review of identity provider, VPN, and cloud logs by the IT Manager, and alert-driven review by a managed detection service, start 2027-01-15.
Servers and endpoints synchronize time with the cloud provider and domain time sources.
Logs are readable only by administrators. Gap: the same administrators can delete them.

provider_if_inherited: Cloud provider; identity provider; ERP vendor
implementation_statement: Logs keep default retention of 30 to 90 days. Gap: too short for investigations or for preserving data for 90 days after a DIBNet report (DFARS 252.204-7012(e)). Target: 1 year in a central log store.
Log generation is on for cloud, identity, firewall, and ERP. Gap: not on for file server object access or the WMS application.
An independent assessor assessed 25 controls from 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-07 (P07). The gap analysis (P03) assessed all 110 SP 800-171 requirements. Both are repeated annually.
evidence: P07 assessment plan; P03 gap analysis

implementation_statement: The POA&M (P07 poam.csv) tracks every weakness with an owner, milestones, and dates. The IT Manager updates it monthly.
Planned. Monthly review of the POA&M, open risks, and security metrics by the Chief Operating Officer starts 2026-11-30.
Windows endpoints use a standard image. Gap: no documented baseline for servers, the firewall, or lab workstations.
Planned. Changes are not logged or approved today. A change log with IT Manager approval and a security impact question starts 2026-11-30.
Endpoint configuration policy enforces screen lock, firewall, and antivirus. Gap: server, firewall, and lab workstation settings are not documented or hardened to a standard.
Only the VPN is open inbound. Gaps: outbound traffic is allowed to any destination, and lab workstations have open internet access.
The RMM tool lists Windows endpoints and servers. Gap: network devices, handhelds, printers, and cloud services are missing, and no asset has a CMMC asset category (32 CFR 170.19(c)).
Office users cannot install software. Gap: lab technicians install tools because they are local administrators.
Planned. No contingency plan exists. A plan built from the BIA (P05), with downtime procedures for order capture and fulfillment, is due 2026-12-31.
regulatory_driver: None (business requirement: P05 BIA; reseller availability commitments, P09 A1.2 and A1.3)

implementation_statement: Planned. Backups have never been restore-tested. Quarterly restore tests start 2026-10-30 and an annual plan exercise starts 2027-03-31.
regulatory_driver: None (business requirement: P05 BIA; reseller availability commitments, P09 A1.3)

implementation_statement: The WMS database and file server are backed up nightly to a backup vault. Gaps: backups share the production cloud account and administrator roles, are not immutable, and give a 24-hour RPO against the 4-hour BIA target. The ERP, portal, and EDI data are backed up by their vendors.
evidence: Backup job history; cloud IAM export

implementation_statement: Planned. No recovery procedures exist. Rebuild and restore procedures for the WMS and file server are part of the contingency plan (2026-12-31).
regulatory_driver: None (business requirement: P05 BIA; reseller availability commitments, P09 A1.2 and A1.3)

implementation_statement: Users sign in to email, ERP, VPN, and the cloud console with unique identity provider accounts. Gap: 6 shared zone accounts on the WMS handhelds.
evidence: Identity provider user export; WMS user list

implementation_statement: All administrator accounts sign in through the identity provider with MFA (authenticator app; hardware keys for the IT Manager and Systems Administrator). The MSP signs in to the RMM tool with MFA.
evidence: Conditional access policy; RMM login settings

implementation_statement: MFA is required for email, ERP, VPN, and the cloud console. Gaps: no MFA for network access to the file server (CUI share) from the office network, and none for the WMS.
Identifiers are unique and never reused. Gap: identifiers are not disabled after 90 days of inactivity (11 accounts unused for more than 90 days were found).
Passwords are at least 14 characters, checked against a banned-password list, and stored hashed by the identity provider. Temporary passwords must change at first use.
Planned. No incident response test has been done. A tabletop of the P08 runbook is due 2026-11-30.

POL-03 and the P08 runbook for supplier compromise and counterfeit products were approved 2026-08-31. Gaps: no forensic retainer beyond the insurer panel, no detection capability, and the runbook is untested.
Planned. Incidents are not tracked. A Security category in the ticketing system starts 2026-10-31.
Planned. The company has no DoD-approved medium assurance certificate, so it cannot report through DIBNet (DFARS 252.204-7012(c)(3)). The certificate and reporting procedure are due 2026-10-15.
POL-03 and the P08 runbook form the incident response plan (approved 2026-08-31). Gap: not yet tested or distributed to the MSP.
Server and network maintenance is scheduled and recorded in MSP tickets.
Gap: there is no approved list of maintenance tools, and lab diagnostic media are not scanned before use.
MSP remote maintenance uses the RMM tool with MFA. Gaps: sessions do not time out and do not require approval by company staff.
Outside maintenance technicians are escorted. Gap: escort and supervision are not recorded.
CUI printouts are used in the lab cage. Gap: printed CUI sometimes leaves the cage for the office printer.
Gap: no locked storage for CUI media and printouts in the lab.
Drives are wiped with a verified tool before reuse, and a certified e-waste vendor destroys failed drives with certificates of destruction.
Planned. USB storage is unrestricted on all endpoints, including lab workstations. Blocking USB storage except company-issued encrypted drives for the lab is due 2026-12-15.

The Warehouse and Logistics Manager approves badge access by role. Lab cage access is limited to 9 badge holders: the 6 technicians, the Configuration Lab Lead, the IT Manager, and the Systems Administrator.
Badge readers control the 4 exterior doors and the lab cage. Gaps: truck drivers and visitors enter the dock without escort, and a physical key to the lab cage is not logged.

24 cameras record to a network video recorder with 30-day retention and cover the dock, cage, and doors. The intrusion alarm is monitored by an alarm company. The camera models were checked against the FAR 52.204-25 covered manufacturers on 2026-07-20: none are covered.
Visitors sign a paper log at reception. Gaps: badge logs are kept only 30 days, and drivers at the dock are not logged.
Staff may work from home on company laptops. Gap: no written rule that CUI stays in the lab and the CUI share.
This SSP describes the boundary, environment, and control implementation for the OFP. With the P03 gap analysis, it serves as the SSP required by SP 800-171 R2 3.12.4. Reviewed annually.
POL-05 Acceptable Use was approved 2026-08-31. Gap: signed acknowledgments are being collected (41 of 62 by 2026-08-31).

implementation_statement: Risk tolerance and acceptance authority are set in POL-01 4.4 and the P01 report; the risk register follows SP 800-30 Rev. 1.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Planned. No supply chain risk management strategy exists. The C-SCRM plan (SR-2) includes the strategy, due 2026-11-30.
Background checks are done before hire for all employees, and for temporary warehouse staff through the staffing agency contract.
HR emails IT when someone leaves. Gaps: no same-day disable, and no lab exit checklist for badge, keys, and CUI.
The OFP is categorized Moderate (section 6 of this SSP), with CUI protected at no less than moderate confidentiality.
regulatory_driver: N42-R03 (252.204-7012(b)); 32 CFR 2002.14(g) (CUI at no less than moderate confidentiality)

implementation_statement: The 2026 risk assessment (P01) follows SP 800-30 Rev. 1 and covers supply chain threats. It is updated each July and after major changes.
Planned. No vulnerability scanning is done. Monthly authenticated scans by the MSP start 2026-11-30, with remediation timelines by severity.
Each risk in P01 has a treatment, owner, and due date; High risks were accepted with treatment plans by the Chief Executive Officer on 2026-08-31.
The BIA (P05) ranks business processes. Gap: no criticality analysis of product lines and OFP components; the two single-source product lines were identified only informally.
The MSP and ERP contracts include confidentiality terms. Gaps: no security or CUI requirements in the forecasting, portal, or MSP contracts, and no DFARS 252.204-7012 flowdown where required.

The ERP and portal vendors provide SOC 2 Type 2 reports. Gaps: the ERP vendor has no FedRAMP Moderate equivalency evidence yet holds CUI attachments; the MSP (an External Service Provider handling Security Protection Data) has no customer responsibility matrix; vendors are not reviewed each year.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 reports; FedRAMP Marketplace check 2026-07-15

implementation_statement: The 40 handheld scanners run an operating system past vendor support. They are being isolated on the scanner VLAN and will be replaced by 2027-01-31.

A next-generation firewall protects the internet boundary with no inbound services except the VPN; guest Wi-Fi is isolated. Gaps: the lab bench network is on the flat corporate VLAN, outbound traffic is not deny-by-default, and there is no documented architecture for protecting CUI.
evidence: Firewall rule export; network diagram draft

implementation_statement: All SaaS, VPN, and cloud traffic uses TLS 1.2 or higher or IPsec.
VPN sessions end after 8 hours. Gap: no idle disconnect (target 30 minutes).
Encryption keys for the cloud tenant are managed by the provider key service; VPN keys are generated on the firewall.
Encryption protects CUI in transit (VPN, TLS) and at rest (provider-managed storage encryption). Gap: FIPS validation of the modules in the VPN, file server storage, and lab laptops is not confirmed.
Conference room cameras and microphones show an indicator when active and cannot be turned on remotely.
File server and WMS disks and the backup vault are encrypted at rest by the provider. Laptops use full-disk encryption.
evidence: Cloud storage settings; endpoint encryption report

implementation_statement: Windows endpoints patch automatically; the MSP patches servers monthly. Gaps: no firmware schedule for the firewall and switches, and the handhelds cannot be patched.
Next-generation antivirus runs on all Windows endpoints and servers, updates automatically, and scans files on access and downloads.
Planned. No 24x7 monitoring or alert review. Managed detection and response through the MSP, with 24x7 alerting, is due 2027-01-15.
The IT Manager reads vendor and CISA alerts when time allows. Gap: no record of action and no ticketed follow-up.
POL-01 section 4.11 to 4.14 (approved 2026-08-31) sets supply chain rules. Gap: C-SCRM procedures are not written.
Planned. No written C-SCRM plan. A plan following NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1, covering sourcing, broker approval, receiving inspection, Section 889 screening, and single-source lines, is due 2026-11-30.

New suppliers pass a tax form, credit check, and bank letter, and go on the approved supplier list spreadsheet. Gaps: no authenticity, security, or Section 889 criteria, and no flowdown of FAR 52.204-25 or DFARS 252.246-7008 to suppliers.

Buyers prefer OEM programs and authorized distributors. Gaps: the sourcing order is not written or recorded on purchase orders, 1,260 SKUs have no manufacturer of record, and there is no covered-manufacturer screening.
Planned. The 12 brokers have never been assessed. Broker assessments against industry counterfeit-avoidance criteria are due 2026-12-15; until then DoD jobs use authorized sources only.
Planned. No supplier agreement requires notice of counterfeit parts, compromise, or covered equipment. Notice terms go into purchase order terms by 2026-10-31.
Planned. Receiving checks quantities only. Seal, packaging, label, and serial checks, with OEM serial validation for DoD-bound and broker stock, start 2026-11-30.
Planned. No anti-counterfeit policy or procedures. Detection (serial validation, OEM verification, quarantine) and reporting to the prime, contracting officer, and OEM are part of the C-SCRM plan.
regulatory_driver: DFARS 252.246-7008(b)(1)-(2) (Prime B subcontract); DFARS 252.246-7008(b)(3)(ii) (Prime B subcontract); DFARS 252.246-7008(c) (Prime B subcontract)

control_name: Configuration Control for Component Service and Repair
implementation_statement: Lab technicians load firmware only from OEM support portals. Gap: firmware hashes and signatures are not verified before loading.
Defective units go back to the OEM through RMA; scrapped units go to a certified e-waste vendor with certificates. Configured DoD returns are wiped before disposal.
